name: Digital Lending — Prohibited Pool/Pass-Through Account Pattern
sourceDocument: Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025
section: Paragraph 9 — Loan disbursal, servicing and repayment
confidenceNote: Primary RBI source confirmed. The implementation is a conservative topology policy and does not by itself establish a legal violation or determine whether an exception applies.
clauseText: Loan disbursal is normally made by the Regulated Entity into the borrower's bank account and must not be made to a third-party account, including an LSP account, except where Paragraph 9 permits it. Servicing and repayment occur directly between the borrower and the Regulated Entity without a third-party pass-through or pool account, and third parties must not control the fund flow.
observableGraphCondition: A MoneyEdge with mechanism=POOL_PASS_THROUGH in a proposed graph that contains an Obligation owed to a FINANCING_PROVIDER.
implementationNotes: POOL_PASS_THROUGH mechanism value is set by the deterministic extractor only when evidence clearly indicates funds flowing through a third-party pool/treasury account before reaching the final destination.
The rule requires lending context: an Obligation owed to a FINANCING_PROVIDER. A POOL_PASS_THROUGH edge outside that context does not trigger DL-01.

The regulatory exceptions listed in clauseText (statutory mandate, co-lending, specific end-use) are not handled by this rule and would require manual review if applicable — this rule is intentionally over-inclusive rather than attempting to encode the exceptions, per the project's principle that REVIEW/BLOCK on uncertainty is safer than a false PASS.
